signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish RBA Repricing
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5785, anchored by the strongest leader-to-laggard spread in the G10 scorecard at 1.951%. AUD 1W average performance is +1.225% (n=4) while CHF lags at -0.726% (n=6), creating a clear divergence. The AUD is supported by a +435bp carry premium over CHF and a hawkish shift in RBA bets targeting the 0.7275 level in AUD/USD. In contrast, CHF weakness is building as the SNB holds rates at 0.00% amid a normal volatility regime (VIX 15.2). The pair remains technically supported by the AUD/USD SMA cluster at 0.6964/0.7086. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry advantage and RBA hawkishness dominate the weakening CHF. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: VIX spikes above 25, triggering a sharp safe-haven CHF bid and carry unwind.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs BoJ Verbal Intervention
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.37, holding just below the 160.00 threshold that previously triggered MoF intervention warnings. A +275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains the primary driver, sustaining the pair despite hawkish rhetoric from BoJ Deputy Governor Himino regarding inflation risks. COT data shows specs are net short JPY at -73,641 (pctl 12), while the options market remains cautious with a strong 1M 25d risk reversal at -1.86, signaling high demand for JPY downside protection. The pair is currently testing its SMA20 at 158.76 as support. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry dominance persists while VIX remains near 15.2. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 64% hike priced) 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Confirmed BoJ/MoF intervention above 160.00 forcing a disorderly squeeze of spec shorts.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7184, significantly above its SMA200 (0.6964) and SMA50 (0.7009) trend anchors. CFTC data confirms a crowded long at +49,749 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.78), indicating spec positioning is at the upper decile of its annual range. This institutional bullishness is met by an extreme retail short of 89%, creating a classic institutional-retail divergence. While a -60bp carry advantage over the USD supports the AUD, the momentum is stalling as WoW adds (+4,022) are decelerating compared to the 4W delta (+29,228). This suggests late-cycle exhaustion where retail capitulation would likely be the final push before a correction. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; institutional momentum remains intact despite retail fading the trend. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: LF net delta turns negative while retail shorts cover, signaling a trend reversal.
evidence: AUD COT LF net pctl(52w): 94 (crowded long)

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Macro Headwinds
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3587, navigating a heavy vol regime where IV (11.0%) exceeds HV30 (5.1%) by 5.9 points, indicating a massive volatility risk premium. This suggests the options market is pricing in significant hedging demand ahead of BoE/Fed uncertainty despite a neutral 25d risk reversal at -0.08. Speculative positioning is crowded with a GBP LF net long of +46,070 (pctl 92, z +1.22), leaving the pair vulnerable to a long-unwind if data continues to miss (ESI -9.3). The pair holds above the SMA20/50 cluster at 1.3410/1.3531. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; extreme vol premium and crowded spec longs cap further upside. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: US PCE surprise extension drives a break below 1.3531, triggering a spec long liquidation.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Commodity Reversal + ESI Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD is at 1.3887, currently trading below its SMA20 (1.3918) and SMA50 (1.4050) as oil prices see a war premium unwind. WTI has fallen below $81.00 following Iran-Oman diplomatic progress, which typically weakens the CAD, yet CAD ESI remains strong at +25.3. This positive data outperformance contrasts with heavy speculative shorting (pctl 3, z -2.07), creating an asymmetric setup for a CAD recovery if trade tariff fears subside. The Fed-BoC +150bp carry spread currently favors the USD, limiting the downside for the pair near 1.3840 (SMA200). Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; positive CAD data surprises challenge crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Sustained WTI breakdown below $75.00 invalidating the CAD recovery thesis.
